front.title: Effect Management Protocol (EMP) for Human-Authorized Effects

abstract.t: This document proposes an experimental Effect Management Protocol (EMP) to coordinate human-authorized objectives from planning through execution, observation, recovery, and independent effect acknowledgement. EMP complements, but does not replace, the QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement Protocol (EAP). This document is an initial proposal and does not claim an interoperable implementation.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: An acknowledgement of a completed effect does not itself specify how to achieve an authorized objective. EMP defines a constrained management lifecycle for that purpose. This draft is a candidate for technical discussion, not a deployed protocol specification.

section.name: Terminology

dl.dd: Human authority specifying and authorizing the objective.
Desired effect and measurable acceptance predicate.
Component collecting attributable evidence of resulting state.
Monotonic identifier used to fence stale effect writers.

section.t: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, and SHOULD are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

section.name: Objective Envelope
section.t: An objective MUST bind a unique identifier, principal identity, authorization reference, target, measurable acceptance predicate, permitted operations, prohibited operations, policy version, resource bounds, deadline, revocation conditions, idempotency key, and writer epoch. Missing authorization MUST prevent effectful execution.

section.name: Lifecycle
section.t: Permitted conceptual states are PROPOSED, AUTHORIZED, PLANNED, EXECUTING, OBSERVING, REPAIRING, BLOCKED, VERIFIED, and ABORTED. A transition to VERIFIED MUST require independent acknowledgement of the acceptance predicate through EAP. BLOCKED MUST record the blocking cause, an unblock predicate, and the next safe action. Revocation MUST prevent subsequent unauthorized execution.

ol.li: Executors MUST NOT act outside delegated authorization.
Success MUST NOT be asserted without independent observation and EAP verification.
Implementations MUST durably journal transitions and reject stale writers using fencing.
Replay of an idempotency key MUST NOT duplicate a non-idempotent effect.
Retries MUST be bounded and MUST NOT bypass governance gates.
Independent ready objectives SHOULD continue when another objective is blocked.
Revocation MUST be checked at defined effectful checkpoints.
Irreversible actions MUST have explicit principal authorization.
Failure evidence MUST be preserved for causal diagnosis.
A generated statement or successful API response MUST NOT be treated as proof of the desired real-world effect.

section.name: Example
section.t: A principal authorizes regeneration of a document bundle with verifiable hashes. EMP records the objective, delegates deterministic generation, and requests independent byte-level readback. If the acceptance predicate and EAP verification succeed, the objective transitions to VERIFIED. Otherwise it remains REPAIRING or BLOCKED with durable evidence.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Implementations need authenticated principal identities, least-privilege delegation, replay prevention, durable writer fencing, integrity-bound evidence, bounded retries, revocation, and separation of duties. Personal digital twins additionally require purpose limitation, consent, and data minimization. The precise authentication, cryptographic binding, and wire format are open design questions; this version is not suitable for interoperable production deployment.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests no IANA actions.

section.name: Open Issues
section.t: Future versions need a canonical wire encoding, error registry, authentication profile, exact EAP version binding, formal threat model, test vectors, and an independently tested reference implementation. A patent-disclosure review is required before public submission.
